texts.preamble: Suresh Prasad Gupta & Ors vs Union Of India & Ors on 9 February, 2018 Author: Debangsu Basak Bench: Debangsu Basak 1 February 09, 2018 R.C. W.P. 2595 (W) Of 2018 Suresh Prasad Gupta & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Ors. =-=-=-=-=- Mr.Ashoke Banerjee, Sr. Advocate Mr.Rahul Karmakar Ms.Gargi Goswami, ...for Petitioner Mr. Ashok Kumar Chakraborty, Sr.Advocate Mr. Sanajit Kumar Ghosh, ...for Respondent Mr. Amitesh Banerjee, Sr. Standing Counsel Mr. Sanjiv Kumar Trivedi Mr. Rudrajit Sarkar, ...for Respondent No. 7 (Irctc)
texts.arguments: Learned senior advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that, the petitioners are valid commission agents. Such agency has not been terminated. The petitioners hold valid licence to undertake their activities. Such licence not being terminated and no notice of eviction being issued, the petitioners cannot be evicted. He draws the attention of the Court to the various documents relied upon in the supplementary affidavit as also in the affidavit filed by the Railways in support of his contentions. The Railways and the IRCTC are represented. Suresh Prasad Gupta & Ors vs Union Of India & Ors on 9 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153040736/ 1 Learned senior advocate appearing for the Railways submits that, the petitioners, at best, can claim themselves to be commission agents. However, such agency stands terminated with the attainment of the prescribed age of 60 years. In any event, none of these petitioners have any valid commercial licence to claim that, they are commission agents. He draws the attention of the Court to the various documents annexed to the pleadings of the parties. Learned senior advocate for the IRCTC submits that, his client has not been served with the copy of the writ petition.
